To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
community engagement and patient engagement are both important for designing and conducting a randomized controlled trial with Marshallese Pacific Islanders.
community and patient stakeholders had a significant influence on the design of a randomized controlled trial of a culturally adapted Diabetes Prevention Program intervention.

the engagement of stakeholders from a Marshallese community in a randomized comparative trial testing two Diabetes interventions resulted in a more culturally appropriate and feasible study design and implementation plan.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new method of stakeholder engagement that will be useful for other investigators in designing and conducting comparative effectiveness trials in Marshallese and other Pacific Islander populations.

the development of a model for the engagement of stakeholders in a comparative effectiveness trial testing a community- and patient-centered intervention to improve diabetes outcomes in a Marshallesek Pacific Islander population.
the development and evaluation of a culturally tailored diabetes prevention intervention for the Marshallese community in Northwest Arkansas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stakeholder engagement was successful in influencing the research protocol.
the stakeholder engagement approach described in this manuscript was effective in influencing the design and conduct of this randomized controlled trial.
stakeholder engagement was critical in developing a culturally sensitive, community- and patient-centered research study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stakeholder-engagement process helped to identify the most appropriate research questions to ask and the best way to ask them.
the engagement process resulted in a research protocol and implementation that were responsive to the community's needs, concerns and priorities.
community stakeholders and academic investigators can collaborate to design and conduct high-quality research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the engagement of community stakeholders in the design and implementation of research is critical to the success of the study and the sustainability of the intervention.

community and patient stakeholders can be engaged in the development of research that is relevant to the population and that their involvement can improve the quality of the research and increase the likelihood that the results will be useful and acceptable to the community and patients.
stakeholder engagement is essential for research that seeks to reduce health inequality and disparities.
